title: Spring Boot DevTools

richText: Spring Boot DevTools adds development features such as automatic restart and browser LiveReload.
Add spring-boot-devtools to the development build. It is a module, not a starter.
Keep DevTools out of production deployments. Boot’s repackaging tools exclude it by default.
Fully packaged applications normally disable DevTools. Do not force it on in production.

For Gradle, use the developmentOnly dependency configuration.

richText: DevTools watches directories on the application classpath. The classpath contains the compiled classes and resources used by the application.
Editing a Java source file alone does not trigger a restart. Compile it so the classpath changes.
Restart recreates the application context using a restart classloader. It does not edit an already-running method in place.
Static files and templates normally trigger LiveReload without an application restart.
DevTools also changes some development defaults, such as disabling template caching.
LiveReload asks a connected browser to refresh after a resource changes.
Install a compatible browser extension and connect it to the DevTools LiveReload server.
Browser refresh and application restart are separate actions.
Set spring.devtools.livereload.enabled=false if you do not want the LiveReload server.
Set spring.devtools.restart.enabled=false to stop restart watching. If classloading causes problems, disable restart before startup while diagnosing them.

summary: Restart a development application after code changes and refresh the browser with LiveReload.
